Alright, let me think this through. I'm old enough now that I've seen plenty of good years and bad years on this land.

---

## My thinking (as the farmer)

I'm 62, been farming this patch for 40 years. My wife and I are the only ones left at home — the kids went to the city long ago and send money sometimes, but the farm is my responsibility. 16 mu is not big, not small. Enough to feed us and sell some grain, not enough to get rich.

I finished middle school, so I can read the bag and I understand what the extension guy (农技员) says when he comes through the village. But I trust what I've seen on my own fields more than anything in a pamphlet. Forty years tells you more than any book.

**About the wheat (already in the ground since last October):**

I planted my usual local variety — 济麦22 type stuff, same as most of the village. Put down a compound fertilizer (复合肥) before sowing, about 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15 type — that's my base. Now it's late April, the wheat is at jointing (拔节), already greened up. I watered it once at returning-green (返青水) in March. Soon I need to topdress urea (追肥) and give it another irrigation — that jointing water (拔节水) is the most important one, everybody in the village knows this. If I skip it the grain will be small.

I'll put down maybe 10 kg of urea per mu now. My neighbor老李 sometimes does 15 but I think that's too much — expensive, and in a wet year it just goes into the air or runs off. I've found 10 kg is enough if the wheat looks green. If it looks yellow I'll add more, but this year it looks fine.

One more irrigation at grain-filling (灌浆水) if it doesn't rain. That's three waterings total for wheat this year — normal.

Weeds I sprayed in February when it warmed up, a bit of 2,4-D type stuff. For aphids and rust I'll watch in May. Last year I had to spray once for aphids. Usually I mix the insecticide with a foliar spray.

Expected yield: if the weather cooperates, maybe 450 kg per mu. Last year I got 430. The year before, 480 — that was a good year. I don't promise myself anything over 500 — that's business-farm territory, not for me.

**About the maize (will plant in June after wheat):**

Wheat comes off around June 10-12. Maize has to go in within a week or the season gets too short. I'll hire the combine for wheat harvest (收割机, about 60 yuan/mu), then right away hire the seeder for maize — no-till into the wheat stubble (免耕直播). Everybody does it this way now, much easier than the old days when we had to till first.

I buy hybrid seed every year — 郑单958 or similar, whatever the seed shop has at a reasonable price. Around 7-8 yuan per kg, I use about 2.5 kg per mu. I don't save maize seed, everyone knows hybrid you have to buy new.

For fertilizer on maize: I used to side-dress (追肥) at the knee-high stage but these past few years I've been using the slow-release compound that you put down once with the seed. Less work for me — I'm not getting younger, and my wife's back isn't good. Maybe 50 kg per mu of a 28-10-8 compound. That works out to about 14 kg N, 5 kg P, 4 kg K per mu. Some farmers add a bit of urea later if the maize looks weak, I'll decide based on how it looks in July.

Irrigation for maize: usually one watering at tasseling (抽雄) if July is dry. Sometimes two. Depends on the rain. Last year I didn't irrigate maize at all — July was wet. Year before I watered twice.

Pesticide: herbicide right after sowing (莠去津-type, atrazine). For corn borer (玉米螟) I use the granule stuff dropped in the whorl in July. Not every year — only if I see them.

Expected yield: 500 kg per mu is what I aim for. Last year 510. I've seen 550 in a great year but don't count on it.

**Money thinking:**

Irrigation is the thing I watch most carefully. Well water costs money — electricity for the pump, about 30-40 yuan per mu per watering at my depth. That adds up. If I can skip one irrigation because of rain, that's real savings.

I don't buy expensive inputs. No drone spraying (无人机), no drip irrigation, no fancy stuff. My 16 mu doesn't justify it and I don't have the capital to invest in machinery — I rent what I need. Family labor is just me and my wife. We can handle it except for harvest and planting, where the machine does the work.

Total input costs for the year for both crops on 16.1 mu should land somewhere around 11,000-12,000 yuan. That leaves some profit if prices hold, less if the government wheat procurement price drops again like people have been worrying about.
